subject: Seahorse model elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation and next steps
messages:
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@quantahealth.com
Date: 2028-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SEV2 — Seahorse (seahorse-lite) 5xx surge starting 09:08 PDT

Team / Quanta platform,

We started seeing an uptick in 5xx responses and short timeouts from the Seahorse (seahorse-lite) family at ~09:08 PDT. Initial indicators:
- Error rate: 5xxs rose from baseline 0.1% to ~6.4% over a 4-minute window.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (primary), /v1/chat (secondary).
- Percentile latency for successful requests remained in range, but a subset saw socket/timeouts.

Immediate actions in-flight:
1) Rolled low-latency traffic to a fallback model variant (seahorse-lite-v1-fallback).
2) Scaled dedicated inference backends for seahorse-lite by +30% and paused batching heuristics that were queuing long contexts.
3) Started log aggregation (attached: seahorse-metrics-05-03.csv) and exported kernel/gpu traces for the 09:05–09:30 window.

We will follow up with a customer-facing note in ~30 minutes once we have confirmation on mitigation.

Apologies for the disruption — will continue to loop you in.

--
Dev Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- seahorse-metrics-05-03.csv (CSV, 120KB)

Subject: Re: SEV2 — Seahorse (seahorse-lite) 5xx surge starting 09:08 PDT

Sarah / team — quick update from Redwood: we observed a transient surge in 5xx and some generation timeouts from the Seahorse-lite family this morning. We've routed live traffic to the fallback variant and applied a temporary batching policy change. Early metrics show the 5xx rate declining toward baseline (~0.5%).

What this means for Quanta:
- You may have seen a small number of failed calls between 09:08–09:22 PDT.
- We do not believe any persistent data loss occurred; requests that failed did not get persisted.
- No change required on your side; we keep the fallback in place for another hour while we validate.

Next steps:
- We will share the aggregated logs and a draft post-incident write-up by EOD (attached when ready).
- Monica will coordinate a short walkthrough if you prefer a quick technical briefing.

If you saw specific examples of failures (IDs/timestamps), send them and we will prioritize review.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Seahorse post-incident: findings, action items, closure

Sarah / Quanta team — thanks again for patience while we completed analysis. Summary and next steps below.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2028-05-03 09:08–09:22 PDT. Peak error rate at 09:12.
- Impacted model: seahorse-lite (inference path kernel mismatch under certain long-context batching patterns).
- User impact: ~0.9% of QuantaHealth traffic observed 5xx responses (total ~43 failed requests); the majority of customer requests were served normally.
- Root cause: an optimizer kernel introduced in a recent runtime patch created a mismatch in KV cache handling when batch sizes grew above a threshold with long prompt contexts. This manifested as transient internal server errors during late-stage tokenization/kv lookup.

Technical details and evidence (high level):
- We validated the kernel path with trace export; attached aggregated logs (seahorse-5xx-aggregated-logs.zip) include per-request traces and correlated GPU kernel IDs for the 09:05–09:30 window.
- Example request IDs (safe to reference): rq-20280503-09-1123, rq-20280503-09-1178 (these returned 5xx and are safe to retry — they were not persisted).

Remediation already applied:
1) Reverted the optimizer kernel that triggered the mismatch.
2) Hardened the batching policy: long-context batching disabled for seahorse-lite until further testing.
3) Expanded automated integration tests to include a long-context KV cache regression suite.
4) Deployed a runtime health check that will divert traffic to fallback variants earlier if error rate exceeds 1%.

Action items & timelines:
- Dev: finish postmortem doc and publish internal + customer copy by 2028-05-07 (attachment: seahorse-postmortem-draft.md).
- SRE: add the failing kernel ID signature to anomaly detectors by 2028-05-09.
- AE/CS (Priyom/Monica): schedule a 30-minute technical briefing with Quanta (if requested) in the next 72 hours.

Customer notes / retry guidance:
- It is safe to retry requests that returned 5xx; there are no side effects or partial writes from our side.
- If you require idempotency guarantees, please use your existing idempotency key header and we will preserve behavior.

Attachments (included):
- seahorse-5xx-aggregated-logs.zip (log bundle, ~2.3MB)
- seahorse-postmortem-draft.md (customer-facing narrative)
- seahorse-metrics-05-03.csv (time series slice)

If you'd like the walkthrough, Monica and I are available tomorrow afternoon; let me know a window. Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the chance to improve the runtime.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
